input.rationale: With only 3 merit shots, I tested two regions: Bi-V-rich near the BiVO4 line (121) and Bi-poor, V-rich near the Cu:V ≈ 1:2 (CuV2O6-like) ratio (54). The V-rich region gave ~45x higher photocurrent. The last shot went to a nearby composition with slightly less Bi and Cu:V ≈ 0.5 (148), which gave the highest photocurrent: 3.15e-5 A.

rejected.reason: Measured 6.3e-7 A, far lower. The BiVO4-like region with ~24% Cu performs poorly.

content.text:
I submitted **index 148** (Bi 0.10, Cu 0.30, V 0.60) as the best composition. It gave a photocurrent of **3.15×10⁻⁵ A**, the highest of the three I measured. I can't tell how close that is to the best in the library.

There were 188 candidates and only 3 photocurrent measurements, so I tested two regions first and then made one small step:

| Index | Bi / Cu / V | Photocurrent (A) | Why I picked it |
|---|---|---|---|
| 121 | 0.39 / 0.24 / 0.37 | 6.3×10⁻⁷ | Close to BiVO₄ (Bi:V 1:1), a well-known photoanode, with little Cu |
| 54 | 0.11 / 0.29 / 0.61 | 2.82×10⁻⁵ | Little Bi, lots of V, Cu:V near 1:2 (like the Cu–V oxide CuV₂O₆) |
| **148** | **0.10 / 0.30 / 0.60** | **3.15×10⁻⁵** | Close neighbour of 54 with slightly less Bi |

- **The V-rich, low-Bi corner is much better.** It gave about 45 times the photocurrent of the BiVO₄-like composition.
- **The last step was cautious.** Moving from 54 to 148 gained about 12%. The rest of that corner (for example 93, 113 and 101, with even less Bi or more V) was never measured, so a better composition there is possible.
- **I didn't use the XRD budget (5 scans).** A crystal-structure scan wouldn't have produced a scored measurement, and with 3 shots I decided it wasn't worth it. So I haven't confirmed that the best samples actually contain CuV₂O₆; that remains an inference from the Cu:V ratio.
